knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A verbal change is confirmed in the agreed channel, so it is traceable and the team can act on it.
One channel keeps schedules, changes and issues traceable. It is a working practice, not a regulatory requirement.
Out-of-scope requests are referred to the supervisor and are not agreed at the door.
The who needs to know section says the building manager or client needs the schedule, the changes, the access arrangements and any incident.

practicalCriteria: Lists the stakeholders for a sample site, with what each needs to know and the channel that reaches them.
Confirms a simulated verbal change in the agreed channel with the time, reason, area and approver.
Refers a simulated out-of-scope request to the supervisor without agreeing it.
passRule: Stakeholders listed, change confirmed in the channel with all required fields, and out-of-scope request referred. Observed in a role-play. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Stakeholder list for a sample site
Channel record showing the confirmed change
Referral note for the out-of-scope request
stopWorkCriteria: Change acted on without confirmation in the channel
